subject.title: [Feature]: Support arbitrary workspace files in bootstrap context injection

question: Should OpenClaw accept explicitly configured custom-basename bootstrap files as a core `bootstrap-extra-files` hook contract?
rationale: This changes deterministic system-prompt context and the effective workspace file-loading contract, which is a product/security boundary choice rather than a mechanical bug fix.

options.title: Approve guarded custom-basename loading
options.body: Allow explicitly configured custom-basename files through the existing hook path after the linked PR or a replacement is rebased and preserves guards, budgets, filtering, and docs.

options.title: Keep recognized basenames only
options.body: Reject arbitrary workspace-file injection and close or redirect custom-file requests to narrower first-class filename or workspace-convention proposals.

options.title: Defer to a broader context API
options.body: Keep the issue open as product design work until maintainers choose a more general context-file contract.

recommendation.title: Approve guarded custom-basename loading
recommendation.body: Allow explicitly configured custom-basename files through the existing hook path after the linked PR or a replacement is rebased and preserves guards, budgets, filtering, and docs.

likelyOwner.reason: He merged the original bootstrap-extra-files feature and is the clearest routing candidate for a core context/config contract decision.
